title: Polyglot proxy for multi-version toolcall + streaming migration
creator: Miguel Ortega
description:
Problem: We have multiple active API surface variants for streaming frames and tool/function calling that differ in handshake, chunk framing, and structured-output annotations. Customers using older SDKs or pinned client libraries observe contract drift when we enable newer streaming semantics. This manifests as truncated tool invocations, mismatched function arg shapes, and downstream parsers failing on structural markers.

Goal: Build a lightweight, runtime-side polyglot proxy that can accept incoming requests in either v1 or v2 API envelope and normalize them to the chosen execution path while preserving an audit trail and reversible mapping. The proxy should be toggleable via behavior flags, support per-customer mode (legacy|converge|strict), and drive a safe migration path with traffic probes and canaries.

High-level approach: Implement a middleground proxy in front of the serving runtime that performs three responsibilities: 1) normalize streaming frames (handshake, event types, EOF markers) so legacy clients can interoperate with new streaming; 2) translate function/tool call payloads between schema variants and add compatibility wrappers for structured outputs; 3) record a compact replay payload (replay-lite) for drift analysis and regression tests. The proxy will be implemented as a small stateless service (polyglot-proxy) deployed in the edge tier with a config store for per-customer behavior flags.

Trade-offs considered: 1) Doing ad-hoc client shims in SDKs vs. central proxy: SDK changes are more permanent but slower to roll out; proxy allows immediate mitigation with per-customer control. 2) Full fidelity replay vs. compact replay-lite: full replay is heavy on storage; replay-lite captures message diffs and metadata sufficient for automated regressions. 3) Inline translation vs. secondary transform: inline keeps latency tight but increases proxy complexity; we accept small tail latency (+5-12ms p95 for typical 512-token flows) in exchange for faster rollout and greater control.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy can accept both v1 and v2 streaming envelopes and emit normalized frames to the runtime with <15ms median added latency on a 512-token profile
Tool/function call events from legacy clients are transformed into v2 invocation schema and result mappings are reversible for logging/telemetry
Per-customer behavior flag exists and can be toggled without service restart via config API
Replay-lite artifacts are produced for 100% of proxied requests and stored to the migration-analysis S3 bucket with size <1KB per request on average
Integration tests covering: streaming frame variation, interleaved tool calls within streams, structured output annotations, and error-paths (mid-stream cancellation, partial tool args)
Canary rollout plan in place: 0.1% shadow -> 1% active -> 10% active with automated regression gates and rollback hooks

comments: 2026-02-12 Miguel Ortega: Initial ticket created after PM triage. Observed multiple customer support tickets showing mismatch between older client libraries and new streaming framing. Linked initial incident notes in Confluence.

2026-02-16 Aisha Kumar: Spike completed. Implemented a PoC proxy that translates handshake and basic frame types. PoC shows ~8ms median latency on local 1-GPU runtime for 256-token flows. Pushed PoC branch to github: github.com/redwood-inference/polyglot-proxy/pulls/12

2026-02-22 Miguel Ortega: Decision: prioritize central proxy to unblock customers quickly. Agreed on replay-lite (diff+metadata) rather than full audio/trace dumps to reduce storage and privacy exposure. Noted need for KMS for storing mapping tables with PII sensitivity in the future.

2026-02-28 Design review (Slack): UX for per-customer flags reviewed with Console team. Need admin audit log entries for every flag toggle. Action: Console PM to add audit API endpoint. Ref: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/PROXY+Migration+Notes

2026-03-03 QA update (Ravi Patel): Added e2e tests for interleaved tool calls inside streaming. Found a failure mode when a v1 client sends a partial tool arg then reconnects; created sub-task ENG-82348 for graceful resume handling.

2026-03-07 Security note (Leah Sun): Per-customer mapping table may contain user-supplied keys from function args. Marked security_review_required=true and added threat-model doc. Link: drive.redwood.com/proxy-security-model

2026-03-10 Aisha Kumar: Performance run in staging: p50 added latency 5ms, p95 18ms (512 tokens, bursty traffic). Memory usage per proxy pod within budget. Preparing canary orchestration template and alert thresholds (error rate increase >0.5% OR user-visible regression >0.2% triggers rollback).
open_questions: How to version the mapping table schema in a backwards-compatible way? (option: schema vtag + migration job)
Should we attempt SDK-side warnings for customers in 'legacy' mode, or rely solely on server-side behavior flags?
What data retention policy for replay-lite artifacts balances debugging needs vs. cost and privacy?
implementation_notes: Proxy will be implemented as Go service using grpc for control and HTTP/2 for streaming frames. Use protobuf v2 for canonical model and a lightweight adapter layer for legacy JSON envelopes.

Mapping algorithm: best-effort field remapping with fallback to pass-through for unknown keys. Attach a transform header mapping: original-field -> canonical-field. Record deltas in replay-lite to enable automated test generation.
Testing: add a new fixture set to the replayer that randomly mutates frame sequence order, injects partial tool args, and simulates client reconnects. Integrate into CI with nightly regression runs.
Rollout: automated canary orchestration using runtime feature flags and traffic-splitting via the router. Canary gating based on both internal (runtime) and external (customer-facing) metrics.
Telemetry: emit mapping-coverage metric (percent of fields translated), transform-errors, and replay-success-rate. These help decide when to flip default behavior for all customers.
